A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain six readable pages, including Figure 1, Table 1, the mathematical formulation, and references. Neither contains appendices. The unresolved citations introduced in v2 do not prevent comparison of the research content.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM English color-naming experiments and simulations of iterated in-context language learning, with outcomes in Figure 1 and Table 1.

after.justification: v2 retains the original LLM color-naming experiments and iterated-learning simulations, including their results in Figure 1 and Table 1.

M1.justification: The models and IICLL procedure remain unchanged: sample color-pseudoword pairs, learn them in context, label the full color space, and transmit labels between generations. The added I-ICL attribution changes the stated provenance without revising these steps.

E1.justification: Both versions retain English naming of 330 colors and artificial color-language transmission, with English, 110 World Color Survey languages, and human iterated-learning data as reference coverage. No datasets, tasks, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: The Gemini-txt, Gemini-img, and Llama-txt comparisons are unchanged, as are the human reference systems, IB optima, and hypothetical-variant counterfactual baseline. The newly mentioned I-ICL framework is not introduced as an evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Both versions specify the same models, randomized presentation of 330 colors, text/image input conditions, naming vocabulary, initialization category counts, and three evaluation measures. No experimental settings or protocols are revised.

E4.justification: The imperceptible input-noise check in Section 3.1 and the analyses of learning trajectories, initialization complexity, and input modality in Section 3.2 are retained unchanged. No ablations or robustness analyses are added.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains averages over ten random seeds with standard deviations, and Figure 1H retains shaded 95% confidence intervals. Neither version changes the reported repetition or uncertainty procedures.

E6.justification: All Table 1 entries are identical, including efficiency losses of 0.68, 0.89, and 0.79 for Llama-txt, Gemini-img, and Gemini-txt, respectively. Figure 1 is also identical, and the reported rankings, trajectories, and qualitative findings are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2 retains the same Gaussian perceptual representation, IB objective in Equation (1), beta constraint, and efficiency-bound formulation. No mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The introduction changes from developing IICLL to extending an earlier I-ICL paradigm, qualifying the contribution's claimed origin. The central claims about efficient, human-aligned category evolution, including the abstract and conclusions, remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Both versions retain the same interpretations concerning model size and category complexity, input representation and generalization, and inductive bias toward efficiency. The suggested extension to other semantic domains and models is also unchanged.

D1.justification: The disclosed model identifiers, input formats, presentation procedure, and generation mechanics are unchanged. v2 adds no implementation settings, hardware information, processing instructions, or code/data access information.

R1.justification: The introduction and Section 3.2 newly position IICLL as building on an earlier iterated in-context learning framework. Both new citations render as '[?]', and the 28-entry bibliography is unchanged, so the intended predecessor cannot be identified from the PDFs.

P1.justification: Two method-positioning passages are locally revised, the acknowledgment changes 'support' to 'supported', and the first-page preprint notice becomes a NeurIPS 2025 conference notice. The document's section order and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Text reflows across pages 2–4; notably, the English-naming results paragraph now begins entirely on page 4 below Table 1. Figure 1 and Table 1 retain identical graphics, captions, structure, and placement.

improvement.justification: v2 potentially improves contribution positioning by acknowledging an I-ICL predecessor, but both new attributions appear as '[?]' without an identifiable bibliography entry. The scientific evidence is unchanged, and the copyediting is limited. The PDFs leave the accuracy and net benefit of the new attribution unresolved, preventing a reliable overall quality judgment.
